jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in Protein Dynamics at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology
jobs.description:
We are offering a three-year PhD fellowship in protein analysis commencing Feb 1, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  Research group
 This PhD project is a collaborative project between the lab of Professor Petrine Wellendorph (Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, specializing in molecular pharmacology, principal supervisor), the Protein Analysis Group of Professor Kasper D. Rand (Department of Pharmacy, specializing in HDX-MS, principal co-supervisor), and Associate Professor Annette E. Langkilde (Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, specialist in SAXS, co-supervisor). This interdisciplinary setup uniquely bridges brain mechanisms with protein dynamics and structure, enabling new biological insights and cross-fertilization between fields. The PhD fellowship is funded by a larger project grant from the Novo Nordisk Foundation.

  Project description
 Neuronal signalling underlies every function of the brain, from basic communication to learning and memory. This project focuses on a calcium-sensing protein that plays a central role in these processes. The project will apply in-solution biophysical and analytical methods to explore molecular details of ligand binding on protein dynamics to promote structure-function of the protein and, ultimately, advance drug discovery. As the primary methodology, mass spectrometry to measure the hydrogen/deuterium exchange (HDX-MS) of the protein in solution will be used. The HDX-MS method has emerged as a sensitive and powerful alternative technology to study the conformation of proteins using only small quantities of dilute samples. The project will utilize HDX-MS to analyze the protein in various conformational and activational states and elucidate its interaction with ligands and other proteins. Furthermore, the project will also use classical radioligand binding techniques and state-of-the-art biophysical methods e.g. DSF and SAXS to measure affinity and oligomerization. This combined experimental approach will allow for a detailed analysis of the biophysical, structural, and pharmacological properties of the protein.

  Principal supervisor
 Professor Petrine Wellendorph, Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, e-mail: pw@sund.ku.dk, tel. +45 3533 6397.

  Start
 1. Feb 2027

  Duration
 3 years as a PhD student

  Place of employment
 The Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology will be the primary host, but the project will also be highly integrated with activities at Department of Pharmacy. Both departments offer research-based education and interdisciplinary research that supports the development and understanding of drugs at the highest level for the benefit of society. We work as part of a dynamic academic community of research, education and innovation within the Pharmaceutical Sciences bridging Health Sciences and Life Sciences.

• Participating in active research environments including a stay at another research team, preferably abroad 	
• Obtaining experience with teaching or other types of dissemination related to your PhD project

• Writing a PhD thesis on the grounds of your project   PhD Programme description
 The PhD programme is a three-year full-time research education within the framework of the 5+3 scheme, intended for candidates holding a relevant academic degree within the project’s subject area (e.g., pharmaceutical sciences, analytical chemistry, biophysics, biochemistry, or related areas).

  Qualifications
 If you have completed your academic education in Denmark, the admission to the PhD programme requires a relevant Master’s degree (equivalent to 180 ECTS BSc + 120 ECTS MSc).

  If you have an academic education from abroad, you must have either a degree equivalent to a Danish master's degree (180 ETCS + 120 ECTS MSc), or at a minimum, a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Danish bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) and be academically qualified at master's level.

  As part of the assessment of whether you meet the educational requirements, you must also achieve a positive academic evaluation and be assessed as the best qualified for the position.

  General criteria:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project (see specific qualifications below) 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Previous publications 	
• The grade point average achieved 	
• Other professional activities 	
• A curious mind-set with an overall interest in protein structure-function 	
• Good language skills in English and, preferably, Danish 	
• A collaborative mindset and strong communication skills   Specific criteria:

  The successful candidate will be an experimentally oriented scientist with a primary interest in protein chemistry, structural biology, mass spectrometry and bioanalytical science. A good understanding of biochemistry and pharmacology is also a clear advantage. Preference will be given to applicants with experience in protein chemistry, mass spectrometry and data analysis. Experience with HDX-MS will give the applicant a particularly strong standing. As the project is highly collaborative, we are looking for applicants who are motivated to work across academic research groups and who bring strong interpersonal and communication skills to this kind of setting.

  Place of employment
 The place of employment is at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. Associated is also the Department of Pharmacy. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories within molecular pharmacology, protein chemistry and mass spectrometry.

  Terms of employment
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 3 years.

  The employment is conditioned upon the applicant’s successful enrolment as a PhD student at the Graduate School at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project to the Graduate School of Health and Medical Sciences.

  The PhD study must be completed in accordance with The Ministerial Order on the PhD programme (2025) and www.healthsciences.ku.dk on achieving the degree.

  The PhD student is expected to be affiliated to the graduate programme in pharmaceutical sciences, www.dra.ku.dk

  Salary, pension, and terms of employment are in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. Depending on seniority, the monthly salary starts at approximately 31,800 DKK/Roughly 4,250 EUR (August 2026) plus pension.

  Application procedure
 Your application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking “Apply now” below and must include the following documents in PDF format:

If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. As a prerequisite for a PhD fellowship employment, your master’s degree must be equivalent to a Danish master’s degree. We encourage you to read more in the assessment database. Please note that we might ask you to obtain an assessment of your education performed by the Ministry of Higher Education and Science. Applicants with a Master´s degree from abroad should also enclose a short description of the grading scale used

  The further process

  The assessor makes a non-prioritized assessment of the academic qualifications and experience with respect to the above-mentioned area of research, techniques, skills and other requirements listed in the advertisement.

  Questions

jobs.occupation: Laboratory technician at DTU Metabolomics Core - DTU Bioengineering
jobs.description:
The DTU Metabolomics Core at DTU Bioengineering, Kgs. Lyngby, is looking for a skilled and motivated Laboratory Technician to join our team of excellent scientists and technicians collaborating on microbial molecules, trying to unravel their importance in nature, and discover how they can benefit humanity in various ways, such as in agriculture, and novel pharmaceuticals.

About the DTU Metabolomics Core
The DTU Metabolomics Core in the Department of Bioengineering is one of a several Core facilities within the Department that supports a wide range of research and teaching. The area in which the Metabolomics Core specializes is in the chemical analysis of small secondary metabolites from microorganisms, such as bacteria, fungi, and microalgae. This analysis is undertaken in our extensive instrument suite (HPLC, LCMS, GCMS, MALDI etc.), a collection of instrumentation that you will work closely with as our new technician.

The primary job areas of responsibility
As Laboratory Technician in the Metabolomics Core, you will play a key role in the day-to-day operation of the facility in close collaboration with the Facility Manager. Your responsibilities will include:

• Operating and maintaining our analytical instrumentation, including high-resolution LC-MS systems (sample preparation, calibration, QC runs, routine troubleshooting and preventive maintenance in cooperation with service engineers)
• Running samples for internal researchers and external contract projects, from sample preparation to data acquisition
• Ordering and managing laboratory supplies, consumables, and chemicals, and keeping the lab stocked and organized
• Maintaining lab standards: cleanliness, safety, waste handling, documentation, and quality control routines
• Supporting users of the facility with practical guidance on sample submission and preparation
• Contributing to the ongoing development of workflows and procedures in the facility
• Supporting students
In addition to this is it expected that you will take part in some Department duties, particularly involving laboratory and chemical safety. This will be done in close collaboration with a team of 4 other technicians working within the same section that hosts the Metabolomics Core.

Qualifications
We expect that you:

• Hold a degree as a laboratory technician (laborant) and/or a BSc/MSc in analytical chemistry, biochemistry, chemical engineering, or a related field
• Have hands-on experience with HPLC instrumentation. Experience with high-resolution MS (e.g., QTOF) is a strong advantage
• Are experienced in routine laboratory work, including sample preparation, solvent handling, and general upkeep of analytical labs
• Have knowledge of Good Laboratory Practice, safety regulations, and documentation standards
• Are structured, detail-oriented, and able to plan your own work independently
• Enjoy collaborating with researchers of different backgrounds and communicating in English (our working language)
• Ideally, have experience with natural products chemistry, and sample preparation
What we offer in return
With this job we offer you an exciting and versatile position in a multicultural, respectful and dynamic research and learning environment with many international employees and students. You will gain hands on experience with a wide variety of different analytical instrumentation and have the freedom to create your own daily agenda by prioritizing your tasks.

You will have:

• A central role in a well-equipped core facility with diverse and exciting projects spanning microbiology, natural products, and industrial collaborations
• Close collaboration with leading research groups at DTU Bioengineering
• A flexible, informal working environment at DTU's Lyngby campus
• Professional development opportunities, including training on new instrumentation and methods
Salary and appointment terms
Salary and appointment terms are in accordance with the OAO-S Joint Agreement and the organization agreement for Office Clerks, Laboratory Technicians and IT staff (HK/stat). In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for clerical employees OR laboratory technicians: https://www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The appointment is permanent full time. The position starts 1st December 2026 or as soon as possible after.

Application and contact
Please submit your online application no later than 4 November 2026. Open the “Apply now” link, fill out the form and attach your motivated application, CV and exam certificates. 

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact Facility Manager, Aaron Andersen by e-mail (ajca@dtu.dk) or by telephone (+45 45 25 61 38). DTU Bioengineering website: https://www.bioengineering.dtu.dk/english.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

jobs.description:
A position as senior researcher (“group leader”) at the Bartholin Institute, Department of Pathology, Centre for Diagnostics, Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen University Hospital is open for appointment from as soon as possible.

The position is combined with a position as professor or associate professor with special focus on translational type 1 or 2 diabetes research at the Biotech Research and Innovation Centre, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

With this position the Bartholin Institute wishes to strengthen the leadership in translational type 1 or 2 diabetes research in collaboration with the University of Copenhagen.

It is a requirement that the applicant is accepted for appointment of both the professorship/the associate professorship and the senior researcher position.

The advertisement for the professorship/the associate professorship is available from the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen Professor or Associate Professor and Research Group Leader with special focus on molecular mechanisms of diabetes

About the department

The Bartholin Institute is an experimental cancer and diabetes research department at Rigshospitalet, Department of Pathology, Centre for Diagnostics. The Bartholin Institute is also affiliated with the University of Copenhagen as part of the Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC). The Bartholin Institute houses three research groups and is situated at Copenhagen Biocenter close to Rigshospitalet and academic institutions.

Research functions and focus areas of the department

The Bartholin Institute is a research department working on various aspects of cancer biology and diabetes. The department covers aspects on cancer growth, recurrence, microenvironment and pathogenesis of diabetes.

Qualifications

For all applicants, regardless of academic background, documentation for competences in the field of laboratory based translational diabetes research should be specified. The capacity of the candidate to integrate research and clinical perspectives is emphasized**. The successful candidate is expected to strengthen and expand the departments research into translational diabetes research. Hence, it is essential that the applicant has a proven track-record within this area. The applicant is expected to establish a cutting-edge research program with clear translational potential and should also have demonstrated the ability to attract external funding to sustain such a program.

Conditions

In order to be considered, the applicant must send an application to both the Faculty (the professorship or the associate professorship) and to the hospital (the senior researcher position) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the professorship/associate professorship. Appointment is conditioned by the fact that the applicant obtains both positions. This also applies to the applicants who are already employed at Copenhagen University Hospital - Rigshospitalet.

Salary and conditions are as agreed between the Danish Regions and the relevant trade union and between the Capital Region/Region Zealand and University of Copenhagen.

As professor at least 50 % of the working time will be allocated to academic tasks (e.g., research, teaching, evaluation tasks and communication with the public) in agreement with the Director at the

Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC). The remaining time will be allocated for other tasks at the Bartholin Institute and the Department of Pathology (e.g. research administration, personnel responsibility, methods establishment and development, grant writing and the establishment of a competitive research group) in agreement with the Head of the Bartholin Institute. The professor will receive a start package covering the salary of 1-2 group members and technical support equivalent to 50 % of a full-time technical position from the Bartholin Institute. Additional support and details on the working conditions must be negotiated with the Head of the Bartholin Institute, Rigshospitalet.

• Curriculum Vitae and a complete list of publications

• A research plan, describing how the applicant sees him/herself contributing to the Bartholin Institute

We're the infrastructure behind the Internet of Things (IoT). Companies building connected products come to us for the connectivity that keeps their devices online, anywhere in the world, and for the platform where they manage, monitor, and troubleshoot it themselves.

****Where we sit

****We're somewhere between SaaS and telecom. We sell software, so we move fast, ship often, and care about the user experience. But we also operate inside telecommunications: which is more complex and technical than most software. Our customers are engineers, they ask hard questions and the relationship starts rather than ends at purchase.

That mix also makes us sticky. Most SaaS tools are nice to have. If our connectivity stops, our customers' products stop. That means our business grows as our customers and the industry grows. We've been growing fast and we don't plan to slow down, which is exactly why we need this role.

This role sits at the intersection of commercial strategy, relationship ownership, and value delivery — with clear accountability for Gross Revenue Retention (GRR), renewal management, and account expansion including Net New MRR.

**We are looking for a systems-minded Senior ML Data Engineer to own the offline-to-online feature infrastructure that powers our real-time recommendation and search engines at scale. • Pipeline Orchestration and Transformations: Design, test, and maintain robust Apache Airflow DAGs and modular dbt transformations to automate end-to-end data ingestion and feature generation under strict low-latency SLAs.

• Infrastructure as Code and Reliability: Provision, scale, and automate cloud data infrastructure using Terraform, Docker, and CI/CD pipelines, implementing automated data quality testing and monitoring across all feature syncs.

• Cross-Functional System Design: Partner directly with Data Scientists and Backend Engineers to define online/offline feature contracts, optimize database schemas for sub-second queries, and eliminate training-serving skew for millions of active users.

**What we’re looking for 🌟

****We Imagine That You Have

**

• 4+ years of experience

• Operational Data Pipelines: Proven experience moving batch features from analytical warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake) into low-latency online stores (AlloyDB, Redis, Feature Stores) to serve real-time ML recommendation models.

• Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Deep hands-on experience provisioning, scaling, and managing cloud data infrastructure using Terraform, Docker, and modern CI/CD automation pipelines.

• Pipeline Orchestration & Transformations: Strong track record building, scheduling, and maintaining workflow orchestrations (e.g., Airflow, Dagster) and modular data transformation frameworks (e.g., dbt).

jobs.occupation: Executive Business Partner
jobs.description:
Are you a well-organized, scientifically minded professional who enjoys working across science, operations, and business? Do you enjoy turning plans into action and ensuring that strategic priorities become measurable results?

At Gubra, we are looking for an Executive Business Partner to serve as a trusted partner to our Chief Scientific Officer (CSO) and Research Leadership Team. This is a high-impact role for a scientifically grounded and execution-oriented professional who combines strong business acumen with a hands-on mindset and a proven ability to translate strategic priorities into coordinated action and measurable results. You excel at bringing structure, driving accountability, and enabling organizational performance.

As Executive Business Partner, you will play a central role in supporting the CSO and Research Leadership Team in driving key priorities and ensuring effective execution across the Research organization. Your responsibilities will span leadership processes, OKRs, business planning and budgeting, Board and management materials, communication, and performance follow-up. You will also take ownership of selected cross-functional initiatives and special projects, stepping in where structure, analysis, coordination, or hands-on execution is needed.

The role offers a unique opportunity to work closely with the CSO and Research Leadership Team, collaborate with key stakeholders across Gubra, and make a tangible impact on how we operate, execute, and deliver on our priorities.

Key Responsibilities

• Serve as a trusted business partner to the CSO and Discovery Leadership Team by providing structured analysis, practical recommendations, and hands-on execution support to enable informed decision-making and successful execution.

• Partner closely with the CSO to drive key priorities and ensure alignment across the Discovery Leadership Team.

• Monitor execution of strategic initiatives and roadmaps, track KPIs and key milestones, proactively identify risks, and drive follow-up to ensure delivery.

• Plan, facilitate, and follow up on Discovery Leadership Team meetings, including agenda planning, decision tracking, and ensuring agreed actions are completed.

• Ensure leadership decisions are translated into clear actions, owners, timelines, and communication points.

• Own the OKR process in the CSO organization, including planning cycles, progress tracking, reporting, and follow-up to support organizational focus and accountability.

• Coordinate annual planning, budgeting, forecasting, and resource planning processes for the Research organization in collaboration with Finance and department leaders.

• Lead and coordinate cross-functional initiatives and special projects, taking hands-on ownership from scoping and analysis through implementation and delivery, while ensuring effective stakeholder management.

• Prepare Board, Executive Leadership Team, and management presentations by translating complex scientific, operational, and business information into clear decision-making materials.

• Develop executive communications, organizational updates, and leadership presentations that support alignment, transparency, and engagement across the Scientific organization.

• Identify opportunities to improve business processes and operational excellence, taking ownership of practical solutions that enhance efficiency and organizational effectiveness.

Required Experience

We imagine that you bring a strong scientific foundation combined with business acumen, strategic perspective, structured execution, and excellent stakeholder management. Your experience may come from consulting, biotech, pharma, project management, business operations, business partnering, or a similar role where you have worked across scientific, strategic, and operational priorities.

• PhD, in life sciences, pharmacology, or related disciplines or equivalent scientific experience

• 3+ years of relevant experience in consulting, biotech, pharma or related industries.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to understand the bigger picture, structure complex topics, and translate them into clear recommendations and actionable plans.

• Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex scientific and business information into clear, concise, and impactful materials.

• Strong project management and execution skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple priorities, drive follow-through, and create momentum.

• High proficiency in PowerPoint and Excel, with experience in reporting, performance tracking, and preparing high-quality management materials.

• Ability to take initiative, work independently, collaborate effectively, exercise sound judgment, and handle confidential information responsibly.

• Experience working with senior leaders and across functions in a fast-paced environment.

To succeed in this role

You are a scientifically grounded professional who combines strategic perspective with a hands-on, execution-oriented mindset. You see the bigger picture while being equally comfortable diving into the details needed to move things forward. You thrive on translating strategic priorities into action and creating structure, clarity, accountability, and progress.

You are comfortable navigating ambiguity, taking ownership of complex and varied assignments, and moving between high-level discussions and hands-on execution. You build trusted relationships, influence without formal authority, and know when to challenge, support, and follow through.

Most importantly, you are someone who gets things done. You combine curiosity, sound judgment, and business understanding with a pragmatic approach and are motivated by helping the CSO and Research Leadership Team turn priorities and decisions into tangible outcomes.

Contact and application

Please apply at our website using the ”Apply” button. The deadline is October 27, 2026.

If you have questions regarding practical matters, you are welcome to contact HR Partner, Simone Sparholt at ssp@gubra.dk. Questions regarding role-specific details will be addressed during the interview.

We are looking forward to receiving your application.

About Gubra

Gubra is a disease-agnostic techbio company specialized in peptide-based drug discovery and development as well as preclinical contract research services striving for excellence at all levels. We insist on doing things efficiently – and often differently - to reach the results we aim for. Our vision is to become leaders in the path towards a more sustainable and healthier world. We do that by facilitating the discovery of new medicine, and by acting and inspiring others to fight the ongoing climate and biodiversity crises.

Gubra’s activities are focused on the early stages of drug development and are organised in two main highly synergistic business areas: Biotech and CRO Services. We generate our revenue by performing research for life science companies as well as by partnering projects from our discovery and development pipeline.

Our therapeutic focus is within metabolic and fibrotic diseases, and we specialize in in vivo pharmacology, ex vivo assays, drug profiling, histology, stereology and whole brain and organ imaging. In addition, we offer a full palette of advanced transcriptomics. Our ML/AI-driven peptide drug discovery platform streaMLine enables us to rapidly develop a peptide hit into a non-clinical candidate ready for development. Through a constant focus on high quality, scientific excellence, speed, and solid teamwork we have established ourselves as a highly professional and competent partner in the market.

People are our greatest asset, and our team consists of around 300 employees of which many are located in Hørsholm, Denmark. The mix of people from different cultures and educational backgrounds combined with our entrepreneurial mindset have greatly impacted our working environment, which is characterized by entrepreneurial drive, scientific curiosity, and teamwork – we join forces!

jobs.occupation: Build your career in Transfer Pricing - Copenhagen
jobs.description:
Company Description

With more than 3000 employees Deloitte is the largest audit and consultancy firm in Denmark. We tailor solutions across Audit, Tax, Financial Advisory Services, Enterprise Risk Services, and Consulting.

About the team

Join our Transfer Pricing team of more than 45 colleagues in Copenhagen and Aarhus. We help international and Danish businesses turn complex tax, finance and operating-model questions into practical solutions. You will build your expertise through real client work, structured learning and close collaboration and help clients navigate tax and transfer pricing challenges.

Job Description

You will work on a wide range of transfer pricing projects across various sectors. Together with your colleagues, you will help clients manage operational transfer pricing matters, audits and compliance, and provide both global and local advice. You can expect a steep learning curve, and  responsibilities that grow with your experience - supported by structured onboarding, regular feedback and close collaboration with experienced colleagues. Alongside your client work, you will have opportunities to attend training in Denmark and at Deloitte University in Paris, strengthening both your technical expertise and client-facing skills.

Ready to take the next step in your career? In this role, you will be involved in:

• Collect and analyse financial and business data for transfer pricing projects across sectors.

• Prepare transfer pricing documentation, benchmarking analyses and intercompany agreements.

• Support audits, international tax requirements and country-by-country reporting.

• Turn your analysis into clear client advice, join client meetings and follow up on agreed actions.

• Contribute ideas to proposals, AI-enabled tools and practical improvements to how we work.

We work in a dynamic, international environment with an informal tone, where quality, collaboration and different perspectives are central to how we create value for clients and for each other.

AI-enabled and digital tools are a natural part of how we work. You will learn to use them responsibly to explore data, support research and benchmarking, improve workflows and strengthen deliverables. No prior AI expertise is required - curiosity, sound judgement and a willingness to learn matter most.

We value the community that extends beyond client work. Our employee association brings people together throughout the year - from social events to shared experiences that cut across teams and business units. We celebrate the wins, big and small, and make a point of recognising individual and shared milestones

The role is full-time, and we are looking for professionals for our offices in both Copenhagen and Aarhus, Denmark.

Qualifications

We are looking for Consultants and Senior Consultants with 0–3 years of relevant experience.

We imagine that you are curious, ambitious and motivated by complex challenges. You take ownership of your responsibilities, collaborate openly with colleagues and clients, and contribute to bringing projects to a successful conclusion.

What you bring to the team:

• A relevant academic background, such as law, economics, finance, accounting or business.

• 0–3 years of relevant experience; internships and student roles are also valuable.

• Analytical, conceptual-thinking and problem-solving skills.

• Curiosity about technology and judgement when using AI-enabled tools.

• Clear communication and an interest in turning complexity into practical advice.

• Good energy and a strong client service instinct

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we still encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can make an impact on our team.

Additional Information

Do you want to be part of our team?

Click the "I am interested" button above if you are ready to join our team.

Send your CV, grade transcript and application in which you present yourself and elaborate on your motivation for pursuing a career in Transfer Pricing and/or highlight relevant projects or previous experience by 5 November 2026. We regularly call for interviews, so send your application already today.

Please do not hesitate to contact Partner Cecilie Emilie Rendtorff at +45 26 61 53 93 or Aske Haahr Lauridsen at +45 20 41 35 92 if you have any questions about the position.

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

By applying for this job, you will be assessed against the Deloitte Global Talent Standards. We have designed these standards to provide a consistent and exceptional Deloitte employee experience globally.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

jobs.description:
Do you want to help facilitate and grow the semiconductor and chip ecosystem in Denmark and beyond, working with the leading researchers in the field, and to turn potential into opportunities, partnerships and projects? Then this job could be for you.  

About the position 

SDU Microelectronics at TEK, headed by professor Farshad Moradi, is part of the Danish Chips Competence Centre (DkCCC) - the new Danish hub for chip technology and your strategic platform. The position offers an opportunity to play a central role in strengthening Denmark’s chip ecosystem and to help connect the ecosystem with fast-growing application areas such as drones, robotics, sensors and autonomous systems, where advanced chip technology is becoming increasingly critical for performance, reliability, energy efficiency and future innovation. 

You will work closely with SDU researchers, DkCCC partners, Danish universities, companies, incubators, industry organizations, funding advisers and European chip networks. Learn more here www.dkccc.eu 

The position involves regular travel within Denmark and occasional travel elsewhere in Europe. 

Your main responsibilities will include:  

• 
Identifying relevant national and European funding opportunities in chip technology, semiconductor development, and chip-enabled applications. 

• 
Developing and maintaining a strategic pipeline of funding calls, project ideas and potential consortium partners. 

• 
Engaging proactively with Danish start-ups, SMEs and established companies to understand their technological needs and funding requirements. 

• 
Connecting companies with relevant researchers, facilities and competencies at SDU and other Danish universities. 

• 
Helping companies and researchers translate technical and business ideas into fundable project concepts. 

• 
Initiating and facilitating Danish and European consortia for chip-related funding calls and identifying opportunities to join existing consortia. 

• 
Promoting Danish chip competencies and contribute to the visibility and strategic development of DkCCC.  

• 
Supporting the full process of funding applications, from project objectives and facilitating consortiums, to coordinating proposals with partners and funding advisers. 

• 
Building relationships with key stakeholders, organizing activities, and events supporting the ecosystem.   

Your profile 
You have a relevant master's degree, for example within engineering or natural sciences, business development or innovation management, economics or business administration, European studies or public policy, research and innovation management, or another relevant field. 

You have documented experience in one or more of the following: 

• 
National or European research and innovation funding 

• 
Development of collaborative funding proposals 

• 
Consortium building and partner identification 

• 
University–industry collaboration or innovation/business development 

• 
Supporting start-ups, SMEs or deep-tech companies 

• 
Stakeholder management and professional networking 

We are looking for a colleague who: 

• 
Is proactive and comfortable initiating contact with companies, researchers and potential partners.  

• 
Is a strong relationship builder who can establish trust across organizational and disciplinary boundaries 

• 
Understands both commercial needs and academic interests and can structure complex consortium-development processes, while maintaining momentum towards a deadline 

• 
Communicates clearly with different stakeholders, technical, academia and experts, business 

• 
Works independently and is persistent and solution oriented, while also contributing actively to a team 

Experience with semiconductors, microelectronics, integrated circuits, quantum technologies, photonics, sensors or other deep-tech fields is a significant advantage — though you don't need to be a chip designer. What matters more is your ability to grasp technology-based opportunities, engage technical specialists, and turn complex ideas into fundable partnerships. Knowledge of European research and innovation programs, including EU Chips Act calls, is also an advantage. 

What we offer 

• 
Become part of SDU’s growing environment for microelectronics and chip technology. 

• 
Build partnerships that may lead to new products, technologies, companies, and investments. 

• 
Work directly with promising Danish start-ups, companies and research environments. 

• 
Help create new university–industry collaborations. 

• 
Develop national and European networks within a strategically important technology area. 

• 
Influence the formation of projects from their earliest stages.  

• 
Collaborate with leading researchers and industry specialists, in an international and interdisciplinary environment. 

• 
A role with considerable independence and the opportunity to shape the methods, networks, and activities used to identify funding opportunities and develop consortia. 

Your organizational home will be TEK Innovation, the research support and innovation unit at TEK, where you will have colleagues with similar jobs, supporting emerging ecosystems, as well as funding advisors and project managers. Your academic home with SDU Microelectronics, where you will work closely with professor Farshad Moradi and his team.

Thit Juul Hvid, Head of TEK Innovation, The Technical Faculty at The University of Southern Denmark tjuul@tek.sdu.dk 

Professor Farshad Moradi, SDU Microelectronics, The Technical faculty at The University of Southern Denmark at moradi@sdu.dk
